title: Selling to Carol: why targeting a narrow ICP wins 10x-100x more customers than expected
summary: Jason Cohen argues you cannot speak to everyone, so write for one perfect customer (Carol) with vivid, specific messaging. Because buyers decide by trade-offs, a Carol-focused message also pulls in 10x-100x more people with similar preferences. He shows how to separate ICP data from noise and why turning down non-ICP revenue marks a seasoned founder.

principles.text: Speaking to everyone means saying nothing to everyone; pick one specific customer type and be evocative.
principles.quote: by *not* speaking to a specific customer, you're saying _nothing_ to _everyone_ and thus _everyone_ will bounce off the home page, and never think of you again.

principles.text: Define a concrete perfect customer (Carol) with professional attributes only: her problems, budget, and why she's buying now.
principles.quote: Whatever problems your product solves, Carol has *all* those problems. She has all the problems, she knows she has the problems, she already has the budget to spend on those problems

principles.text: Test messaging against Carol: if the ad can't grab your perfect customer in seconds, it won't grab anyone else.
principles.quote: If your ad can't grab Carol's attention--your perfect customer--why do you think it will grab anyone else's attention?

principles.text: Targeting Carol doesn't shrink your market: people with similar trade-off preferences buy too, making the effective market 10x-100x larger.
principles.quote: your effective target is actually at least 10x larger (because of Diana) and more like 20x-100x larger (because of Eddie).

principles.text: Segment ICP customers in all your data (cancellations, activation, usage, support) and ignore non-ICP noise, or you build for nobody.
principles.quote: If we treat all customers as if they are Carol, and therefore all cancellation data as a vital signal, we lose track of building for Carol and we end up building for nobody.

principles.text: Turn down or let go of big non-ICP customers; chasing their revenue wastes time better spent finding more Carols.
principles.quote: You'll know that you're doing this right when you turn down a sale, even though it would have been your largest customer, simply because they're not your ICP
